definitions.explanation: Thin noodles made from buckwheat flour, served either chilled with a dipping sauce or in hot broth. One of the most iconic Japanese noodle dishes.

examples.japanese: お{昼|ひる}に{蕎麦|そば}を{食|た}べた。
{夏|なつ}はやっぱり{冷|つめ}たい{蕎麦|そば}がおいしい。
examples.english: Cold soba really is delicious in summer.

examples.japanese: {年越|としこ}し{蕎麦|そば}を{食|た}べて{新年|しんねん}を{迎|むか}えるのが{日本|にほん}の{伝統|でんとう}だ。
examples.english: It is a Japanese tradition to eat toshikoshi soba to ring in the new year.

notes:
Distinct from そば (beside, near). This word refers specifically to buckwheat noodles. The kanji {蕎麦|そば} is often written in hiragana on menus.

COMMON TYPES:
- {ざる蕎麦|ざるそば} (chilled soba on a bamboo tray)
- {かけ蕎麦|かけそば} (soba in hot broth)
- {天|てん}ぷら{蕎麦|そば} (soba with tempura)
- {年越|としこ}し{蕎麦|そば} (New Year's Eve soba)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蕎麦|そば}を{茹|ゆ}でる (to boil soba)
- {蕎麦|そば}をすする (to slurp soba)
- {蕎麦|そば}を{打|う}つ (to make soba by hand)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{年越|としこ}し{蕎麦|そば} is eaten on New Year's Eve, symbolizing longevity and cutting off the hardships of the past year. {蕎麦|そば}{屋|や} (soba restaurants) are a staple of Japanese dining culture.
